blocks.x: Revised FY27 Budget: SRO Costs Reallocated to the City
8.1 & 8.2 — Public Hearing on the Revised Budget Warrants

This special meeting existed for one purpose: formally reducing the FY27 school budget after City Council agreed to move the full cost of the district's School Resource Officer (SRO) program out of the school budget and into the City's public safety budget — the reallocation request Chair Mancuso first raised in writing at the April 8 Finance Committee meeting. No members of the public spoke at the hearing.
8.2 (close public hearing, return to session): approved 6–0.
8.3 — Adoption of the Revised FY27 Budget (First Reading, Roll Call Vote)

Chair Mancuso read the specific warrant revisions into the record, touching three articles: Article 3 (additional local funds) reduced from $11,829,489.94 to $11,693,194.55; Article 4 (total budget) reduced from $57,349,321.39 to $57,213,026.00; and Article 4A (regular instruction) reduced from $21,712,387.01 to $21,576,091.62. Each reduction reflects the same $136,295.39 — the school department's former 50% share of SRO salary and benefit costs, now reallocated entirely to the City's public safety budget. Chair Mancuso publicly thanked City administration and City Council for accommodating the change.
Approved 6–0 by roll call (first reading); a second and final reading follows May 4, ahead of City Council's own second and final vote on the combined budget the same evening.
